chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

From Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, the Exalted, said: 'O My servants, I have made oppression forbidden for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another.'
O My servants, all of you are astray except whom I guide, so seek My guidance and I will guide you.
O My servants, all of you are hungry except whom I feed, so seek My food and I will feed you.
O My servants, all of you are naked except whom I clothe, so seek My clothing and I will clothe you.
O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you.
O My servants, you will not be able to harm Me, so you do not harm Me, nor will you be able to benefit Me, so you do not benefit Me.
O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans and the jinn of you, were upon the piety of the heart of one man of you, it would not increase My dominion in anything.
O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans and the jinn of you, were upon the wickedness of the heart of one man of you, it would not decrease My dominion in anything.

O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, the humans and the jiv of you, stood in one plain and asked Me, and I gave every man of them his request, it would not decrease what is with Me except as a needle decreases when a hair is taken from it.
O My servants, your deeds are enumerated for you, then I will recompense you for them. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame only himself.

key_terms.الْخَزِيمَةُ: A she-camel or similar animal, used in simile for negligible decrease

ai.seo_question: What does the Hadith Qudsi say about divine justice and human deeds?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Kamal al-Din*, this Hadith Qudsi underscores the Shia doctrine of *Adl* (Divine Justice) by affirming that God’s decree is rooted in His inherent fairness rather than arbitrary will. It highlights that human accountability is based on free will and deeds, reinforcing the balance between divine mercy and retribution, a key theme in Usul al-Kafi and other primary Shia sources.
